name: appreciation
description: Attractiveness to the senses or sensibilities in purely subjective arena.

variations.name: mental appreciation
variations.description: Something attractive in the mental realm may invoke appreciation and perhaps a desire to share it socially. For example, the recognition of a well-built instance of a favorite architectural style may create a sense of appreciation, and also support an identity as someone who's into that kind of thing.

variations.name: natural appreciation
variations.description: A peaceful nature scene may invoke awe. For example, a bright orange sunset.

variations.name: aesthetic appreciation
variations.description: Bright colors or a musical medley may invoke a sense of beauty. For example, a sunlit stained glass window.

variations.name: appreciation signaling
variations.description: Sometimes we might recognize that a social group expects us to find a certain thing appealing, which may nudge us into paying closer attention.

variations.name: remembered appreciation
variations.description: Music or smells can bring back early formative memories. e.g. For some people, the smell of crayons brings memories of childhood.

variations.name: physical appreciation
variations.description: A particularly attractive item, ideal, or person may create a sense of longing to be more closely associated with it/him/her.

commentaries.quote: Aesthetic appreciation is always subjective. Someone else may not appreciate the architecture, singing voice, sunset, stained glass, or the smell of crayons. They may even have a negative reaction.
There are many reasons we may like or dislike something.

conditions: Something in the mental realm is perceived as closely matching an ideal.
Something in the social environment is perceived as closely matching an ideal held by one of your identities.
Something in the sensory environment matches an ideal represented by an instinct or foundational memory.
